<findings>
<finding task="2"><quote>`exclude-newer` set to the RFC 3339 timestamp of 00:00:00Z on the day after the freeze date | Every `uv run` from the repo root resolves as of the freeze date, script headers included. Files uploaded on the freeze date itself (UTC) are included.</quote><plan>    @property
    def cutoff(self) -> str:
        '''00:00:00Z on the freeze date, so uv resolves as of the start of that day.'''
        return f'{self.freeze:%Y-%m-%d}T00:00:00Z'</plan><fix>Set the cutoff to 00:00:00Z on `freeze + 1 day`. Change the Task 2 tests to expect `'2026-10-20T00:00:00Z'` for 2026-10-19 and `'2027-01-01T00:00:00Z'` for 2026-12-31, and fix the `uv.toml` comment text. Also change every test that hard-codes the old cutoff: the Task 3 bump/resolve tests, the Task 5 `uv_run_argv` and `late_pins` tests (an upload during the freeze date must pass; one at 2026-10-20T00:00Z must fail), and the Task 7 expectations.</fix></finding>
<finding task="0"><quote>`uv.toml` (repo root) | `exclude-newer` set to the RFC 3339 timestamp of 00:00:00Z on the day after the freeze date</quote><plan>**Freeze.** `uv.toml` sets `exclude-newer` to the RFC 3339 timestamp of 00:00:00Z on the freeze date (R2.1).</plan><fix>Copy the spec value verbatim into Global Constraints ("00:00:00Z on the day after the freeze date; files uploaded on the freeze date itself (UTC) are included"). Fix the "Labels used in this plan" definition of **cutoff** the same way.</fix></finding>
<finding task="0"><quote>Every plan MUST start with this header</quote><plan>## Global Constraints

Every task's requirements include this section.</plan><fix>Add the required `## Review Focus` section before `## Decisions`. List the five untested failure modes most likely to bite a user, for example:
- a pin uploaded on the freeze date itself;
- a skill script run through the `~/.claude/skills` symlink while under `skills/uv.toml`;
- a nested worktree that silently inherits the root date;
- a `bump` whose resolve partly fails, leaving the file half-written;
- a citation that wraps across Markdown emphasis.

Then add one test for each line in the task whose code would fail.</fix></finding>
<finding task="0"><quote>`- **D<n>** (owner, <brief | plan review>, YYYY-MM-DD): <decision>. Applied in: <Task N | Global Constraints | Task N (spec amendment)>.`</quote><plan>The owner approved the default for each of Q1 to Q8 at plan review ("Approve defaults").</plan><fix>Two problems here:
1. The handoff still says "The decisions that need you are Q1 to Q8 above", so either the review has not happened or the handoff is stale. Log only decisions the owner has actually taken, and make the two sections agree.
2. The plan's D1–D8 reuse the spec's D1–D8 labels, which the plan itself defines as "the owner decisions in the spec's table". Renumber the plan's decisions (for example D9–D16) or prefix them, so "D2" is not ambiguous.</fix></finding>
<finding task="9"><quote>**Floors.** Each script's `requires-python` must match the Python floor in its `SKILL.md` `compatibility:` line.</quote><plan>- **D4** (owner, plan review, 2026-10-21): Q4. The floors rule fails when a script needs a higher Python than its skill promises or than the dev Python. A lower script floor passes. Applied in: Task 9.</plan><fix>This changes what R4.1.4 requires, so it is spec-level. Add an amendment task with an exact replace-this-with-that block for R4.1 item 4, tagged `(owner, plan 66, 2026-10-21)`, and change the log entry to "Applied in: Task 9 (spec amendment)".</fix></finding>
<finding task="9"><quote>Illustrative text, such as the run manifest at `skills/evaluate-deep-learning/references/experiments.md:86-87`, goes on `HISTORICAL` with a reason.</quote><plan>HISTORICAL: dict[str, str] = {
    'ArviZ 0.23': 'the classic stack, named so the porting tables can map from it to ArviZ 1',
    'arviz-stats < 1.0.0': 'the releases that have no azs.diagnose, which the fallback in diagnostics.md is for',
}</plan><fix>Add an entry for each versioned phrase in the `experiments.md:86-87` manifest, with the reason "illustrative run manifest, not a verified claim". If no phrase there matches a listed name, record that finding in Task 9 Step 6, so the spec's named case is shown to be handled rather than silently omitted.</fix></finding>
<finding task="13"><quote>`build/test_run_suites.py` and `build/test_check_frontmatter.py:434` build their expected commands from the file, not from a `3.13` literal.</quote><plan>The sweep also changed the sample command text in `build/test_check_frontmatter.py` (R7 names its line 434). That test checks only the runner word, so it keeps passing.</plan><fix>Add a step, with a failing test first, that makes `build/test_check_frontmatter.py:434` build its expected command from `versions.load()`, as Task 7 does for `test_run_suites.py`. Do not rely on the sweep deleting the flag.</fix></finding>
<finding task="3"><quote>A joint resolve that fails in `bump` or `drift` names the packages in conflict.</quote><plan>        raise VersionsError(f'resolve step: joint resolve of {", ".join(requirements)} on Python '
                            f'{python_version} failed:\n{done.stderr.strip()}')</plan><fix>Parse uv's "Because …" explanation and name the conflicting packages: the `[packages]` names that appear in stderr. Make the test assert that only those names are listed. Do not list every requirement, since a stderr in which only `alpha` and `gamma` conflict must not report `beta-two`.</fix></finding>
<finding task="0"><quote>A plan more than about five times as long as the spec it implements is a transcript of the program, not a plan: cut it before you save it. Replace code bodies with signatures, test names and assertions</quote><plan>- [ ] **Step 3: Write the module.** Create `build/versions.py`.</plan><fix>Replace the full module bodies with signatures, the values the spec pins, and the tests:
- `versions.py` in Tasks 2, 3, 5 and 8;
- `versions_check.py` in Task 9;
- most of the Task 1 probe script.

Keep code only for algorithms the tests do not determine, such as the citation regex and the `rewrite` line rules. The plan is currently far beyond five times the spec's length.</fix></finding>
</findings>
